Add preselection and complete ac4 parser

Cache each label language size on the box for the preselection copier.

Signed-off-by: Cecilia Chen <Cecilia.chen@dolby.com>

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

Fix memory leaks identified during testing

Copy a preselection label language from the size cached on the box, and keep that width on the box for the later label pass.

Signed-off-by: Cecilia Chen <Cecilia.chen@dolby.com>

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

fuzz: ac4 mem fixes

ossfuzz issues 556288792 555510194 555446688 555786511

When a label box already carries a cached language width, copy that many bytes into the preselection config.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling: The over-read is a one-byte gap between the language buffer labl_box_read allocates (strlen+1) and the width a later memcpy uses. That width is published in two places and consumed in two places, and no single edit does both for the same slot. 9704373 stashes lang_bytes+(lang_bytes>>8) in the spare high byte of version and the top byte of flags. For a short ISO-639 tag the shift is zero so the stash equals the buffer; past 255 bytes it is one past the allocation. Nothing reads the stash in that commit. ce6bad0 copies the language with that stashed width, falling back to strlen+1 when the stash is empty, and for long tags records the same inflated width in internal_flags. With the stash empty its own memcpy is exact, and it does not copy from internal_flags. fd7c0a6 copies the language again, using internal_flags when that field is wider than a byte and otherwise the version/flags stash. With both empty it leaves the strdup'd string alone. Each edit by itself is safe. Each pair over-reads the same public preselection input: 9704373+ce6bad0 (version/flags stash consumed by the leak-fix copier), 9704373+fd7c0a6 (same stash consumed by the second copier), and ce6bad0+fd7c0a6 (internal_flags width consumed by the second copier, with no version/flags stash). Reverting any one diff leaves the other pair intact, so the memcpy still runs one byte past the language allocation. Stopping the inflated publish or stopping one of the trusting copies is not enough; both publishers and both copiers have to be brought back to strlen+1. Short tags never add the extra byte, so ordinary labels still copy exactly.
